newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close firm, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close firm, but off highs.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed firmer but well off highs on Tuesday, dragged back by weakness in propety stocks despite sharp gains on Wall Street overnight and continued buying interest in red chips, brokers said.
The Hang Seng Index ended 46.05 points higher at 12,342.02. Turnover was HK$9.11 billion, against Monday's HK$7.64 billion.
The index retreated steadily in afternoon trade after ending the morning 81.77 points higher.
"Most of the property stocks are coming off," said Michael Ng of Sassoon Securities.
Red chips were again in demand, brokers said.

"I think quite a lot of institutions are looking at the market (for China-related shares) and saying 'oh my God I'm going to miss out if I don't start buying'," said Miles Remington, sales trader with SocGen-Crosby Securities.
The index's early strength was a technical rebound after Monday's sharp selloff, when it lost 220.63 points or 1.76 percent, and Wall Street's overnight rally, brokers said.
Buying interest in index stalwart HSBC Holdings Plc also buoyed the market, brokers said. Late buying saw HSBC up HK$2.00 or 1.11 percent at HK$182.50 at the close.

Brokers said the market would be focusing on Wall Street's reaction to U.S. consumer price index (CPI) data overnight for a clue to whether the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee was likely to raise U.S. interest rates after its May meeting.
Leading the property counters' decline was New World Development which lost HK$1.00 to HK$38.80.

Shares in property group Sino Land Co Ltd fell HK$0.20 cents to HK$7.25. The company reaffirmed it planned to complete the acquisition of a site for a record-breaking HK$11.82 billion on schedule, and proposed a US$130 million convertible bond issue partly to fund the purchase.
Wheelock and Co Ltd was off HK$0.35 at HK$16.10.
Among the red chips, Shanghai Industrial Holdings Ltd was up HK$1.30 or 3.32 percent at HK$40.40, and Citic Pacific Ltd was up HK$1.20 or 3.18 percent at HK$38.90.
China Resources Enterprise Ltd surged to a record high of HK$19.80 before retreating to close HK$0.95 higher at HK$19.35.

Shares in China Light & Power Co Ltd fell HK$0.20 to HK$34.80 after it said delaying bringing its Black Point power station fully onstream could cost between HK$2 billion and HK$3 billion in extra capital expenditure over the life of the plant.
